archetypes.name: token-pricing
archetypes.rationale: The diff migrates cost computation while preserving token-cost.sh as the authority, which is a specialized correctness risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether report token costs, vendor bucket handling, fallback behavior, and rate environment forwarding preserve the intended pricing contract. Pay special attention to paths where Python might recompute headline totals or silently degrade bucketed vendor data. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: quiet-fd
archetypes.rationale: The bash wrapper and Python CLI must preserve stdout/stderr behavior under larch quiet mode.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the shell-to-Python boundary for quiet-mode stream restoration, diagnostics visibility, exit-code propagation, and argument pass-through. Check whether failures that used to be hidden or swallowed now reliably reach the caller without breaking normal command output. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: issue-body
archetypes.rationale: The new GitHub issue posting path combines redaction, byte-limit trimming, repo slug handling, and gh invocation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the report issue creation path for post-redaction byte measurement, truncation safety, secret and tmpdir scrubbing, and loud failure behavior. Check whether repo slug absence or gh failures can still produce misleading URLs, leaked data, or silent success. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: scan-pipeline
archetypes.rationale: The larch-log scanner now decides which runs count and how partial or malformed reports are handled.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate run discovery, manifest parsing, workflow classification, limit handling, and skip-vs-default behavior for design and implement logs. Look for regressions around malformed JSON, missing token data, unknown workflows, duplicate issue numbers, and date semantics. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: plot-isolation
archetypes.rationale: The design intentionally isolates matplotlib outside python/ while preserving a JSON subprocess contract.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether plotting remains isolated from the stdlib-only Python package while still honoring the documented schema and persistent artifact lifetime. Check the subprocess invocation, MPLCONFIGDIR handling, no-plot behavior, child failure handling, and schema drift between producer, plot script, docs, and tests. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: ci-surface
archetypes.rationale: The change expands Makefile, CI dependencies, relevant checks, and harness sharding around a live runtime feature.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the new tests, Makefile targets, CI dependency changes, and relevant-checks routing exercise the migrated report-tokens path without slowing or breaking unrelated shards. Check for missing harness registration, stale phony names, dependency mismatches, and docs that promise checks not actually wired. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
